matched_variant_raw.rewritten_question_text:
Current runs through an aqueous solution of nickel(II) fluoride, and evolves at the right-hand electrode. The standard reduction potentials of several reactions are given as follows:

For the half-cell reaction of fluorine gas, fluorine is reduced to fluoride ions, and the standard reduction potential is $+2.87$V:
$$\text{F}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{F}^-$$

For reducing oxygen in the case of forming water in the presence of protons, the standard reduction potential is $+1.23$V:
$$\text{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

For reducing nickel ions to solid nickel, the standard reduction potential is $-0.25$V:
$$\text{Ni}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Ni}(\mathrm{s})$$

Finally, for reducing water to hydrogen gas and hydroxide ions, the standard reduction potential is $-0.83$V:
$$2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\mathrm{l}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\text{OH}^-$$

Calculate the standard cell potential of this cell. (The final answer is a value)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is an electrolytic apparatus containing NiF2(aq) solution, the left electrode is labeled A, and the right electrode is labeled B; the two electrodes are connected through the external Power Source above. Multiple bubbles are drawn around the right-side B electrode, indicating that gas is generated at the right-hand electrode B. Then reason: According to the method draft, regard the B electrode where gas is produced on the right side as the anode where oxidation occurs. Reduction occurs at the cathode; compare the possible reduction reactions: Ni2+ + 2e− → Ni(s) has E°red = -0.25 V, and water reduction to generate H2 has E°red = -0.83 V; the more positive reduction potential is more likely to occur, so choose Ni2+ reduction to Ni at the cathode. Oxidation occurs at the anode; among the given standard reduction potentials, use the reverse of O2 + 4H+ + 4e− → 2H2O with E°red = +1.23 V to represent water being oxidized to generate oxygen, rather than using F− oxidized into F2. Calculate the standard cell potential according to the reduction potentials: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode(reduction) = (-0.25) - (+1.23) = -1.48 V. Since this is an electrolytic cell, take the magnitude of the required applied standard voltage, so report 1.48 V.

method.method_draft: 先根据图像确认这是外加电源驱动的电解，且右电极生成气体。由给出的电势选择阴极还原为 Ni2+ + 2e− → Ni(s)，因为它比水还原更容易；气体阳极反应取水氧化生成 O2，即把 O2 + 4H+ + 4e− → 2H2O 反向。将镍还原半反应乘以 2，与 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e− 合并，得到总反应 2Ni2+ + 2H2O → 2Ni(s) + O2 + 4H+。用自由能法：镍还原部分对应 E° = −0.25 V，水氧化部分对应 E°ox = −1.23 V；合并后的总 E°cell 等价为 −1.48 V，表示非自发。所需外加标准电势为其大小 1.48 V。
method.CoT_raw:
图像显示一个装有 NiF2(aq) 溶液的电解装置，左右各有一个电极，左电极标为 A，右电极标为 B；上方连接了外加 Power Source，说明这是外加电源驱动的电解池。右侧 B 电极周围画有气泡，表示气体在右手电极处生成。

根据给出的标准还原电位，在阴极发生还原。可还原的主要物种是 Ni2+ 和水：Ni2+ + 2e− → Ni(s), E° = −0.25 V；水还原为 H2 的 E° = −0.83 V。因为 −0.25 V 比 −0.83 V 更高，Ni2+ 更容易被还原，所以阴极反应取 Ni2+ + 2e− → Ni(s)。

右手电极处生成气体，按方法取阳极气体为 O2，即水被氧化。给出的氧气还原反应为 O2(g) + 4H+ + 4e− → 2H2O, E°red = +1.23 V；反向作为氧化反应为 2H2O → O2(g) + 4H+ + 4e−，其 E°ox = −1.23 V。

为配平电子，将镍还原半反应乘以 2：2Ni2+ + 4e− → 2Ni(s)。与水氧化反应相加得总反应：2Ni2+ + 2H2O → 2Ni(s) + O2 + 4H+。

标准电池电位为 E°cell = E°cathode(red) + E°anode(ox) = (−0.25 V) + (−1.23 V) = −1.48 V。这表示该反应在标准条件下非自发，需要外加电压驱动；所需外加标准电势的大小为 1.48 V。

solver_metadata.cot_raw:
图像显示一个装有 NiF2(aq) 溶液的电解装置，左右各有一个电极，左电极标为 A，右电极标为 B；上方连接了外加 Power Source，说明这是外加电源驱动的电解池。右侧 B 电极周围画有气泡，表示气体在右手电极处生成。

根据给出的标准还原电位，在阴极发生还原。可还原的主要物种是 Ni2+ 和水：Ni2+ + 2e− → Ni(s), E° = −0.25 V；水还原为 H2 的 E° = −0.83 V。因为 −0.25 V 比 −0.83 V 更高，Ni2+ 更容易被还原，所以阴极反应取 Ni2+ + 2e− → Ni(s)。

右手电极处生成气体，按方法取阳极气体为 O2，即水被氧化。给出的氧气还原反应为 O2(g) + 4H+ + 4e− → 2H2O, E°red = +1.23 V；反向作为氧化反应为 2H2O → O2(g) + 4H+ + 4e−，其 E°ox = −1.23 V。

为配平电子，将镍还原半反应乘以 2：2Ni2+ + 4e− → 2Ni(s)。与水氧化反应相加得总反应：2Ni2+ + 2H2O → 2Ni(s) + O2 + 4H+。

标准电池电位为 E°cell = E°cathode(red) + E°anode(ox) = (−0.25 V) + (−1.23 V) = −1.48 V。这表示该反应在标准条件下非自发，需要外加电压驱动；所需外加标准电势的大小为 1.48 V。
possible_risk_flags: 标准电池电位若按电解反应本身可写为 -1.48 V；题目标准答案取所需外加电势大小 1.48 V

verify_reports.critic_suggestions: 推理轨迹整体通过。它先描述图像再进行电化学推理，视觉描述与图像一致：NiF2(aq) 溶液、左右电极 A/B、上方外加电源、右侧 B 电极气泡均可从图中验证。化学步骤基本忠于方法草稿：选 Ni2+/Ni 作为阴极还原，选水氧化生成 O2 作为右侧气体阳极反应，配平电子后计算 E°cell = -0.25 + (-1.23) = -1.48 V，并报告外加电势大小 1.48 V，与标准答案一致。若需微调，可在最后更明确说明题目标准答案采用“所需外加电压的大小”，而热力学电池电势本身为 -1.48 V。

raw_record.original_question:
电流通过镍(II)氟化物的水溶液运行,并在右手电极处进化。给出了几种反应的标准还原电位如下:

对于氟气体的半细胞反应,氟被还原为氟化离子,标准还原电位为$+2.87$V:
$$\text{F}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{F}^-$$

用于在质子存在下形成水的情况下还原氧气,标准还原电位为$+1.23$V:
$$\text{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

用于还原镍离子为实心镍,标准还原电位为$-0.25$V:
$$\text{Ni}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Ni}(\mathrm{s})$$

最后,对于将水还原为氢气和氢氧化物离子,标准还原电位为$-0.83$V:
$$2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\mathrm{l}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\text{OH}^-$$

计算该电池的标准电池电位。(最终答案是一个值)
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is an electrolytic apparatus containing NiF2(aq) solution, the left electrode is labeled A, and the right electrode is labeled B; the two electrodes are connected through the external Power Source above. Multiple bubbles are drawn around the right-side B electrode, indicating that gas is generated at the right-hand electrode B. Then reason: According to the method draft, regard the B electrode where gas is produced on the right side as the anode where oxidation occurs. Reduction occurs at the cathode; compare the possible reduction reactions: Ni2+ + 2e− → Ni(s) has E°red = -0.25 V, and water reduction to generate H2 has E°red = -0.83 V; the more positive reduction potential is more likely to occur, so choose Ni2+ reduction to Ni at the cathode. Oxidation occurs at the anode; among the given standard reduction potentials, use the reverse of O2 + 4H+ + 4e− → 2H2O with E°red = +1.23 V to represent water being oxidized to generate oxygen, rather than using F− oxidized into F2. Calculate the standard cell potential according to the reduction potentials: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode(reduction) = (-0.25) - (+1.23) = -1.48 V. Since this is an electrolytic cell, take the magnitude of the required applied standard voltage, so report 1.48 V.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Current runs through an aqueous solution of nickel(II) fluoride, and evolves at the right-hand electrode. The standard reduction potentials of several reactions are given as follows:

For the half-cell reaction of fluorine gas, fluorine is reduced to fluoride ions, and the standard reduction potential is $+2.87$V:
$$\text{F}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{F}^-$$

For reducing oxygen in the case of forming water in the presence of protons, the standard reduction potential is $+1.23$V:
$$\text{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

For reducing nickel ions to solid nickel, the standard reduction potential is $-0.25$V:
$$\text{Ni}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Ni}(\mathrm{s})$$

Finally, for reducing water to hydrogen gas and hydroxide ions, the standard reduction potential is $-0.83$V:
$$2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\mathrm{l}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\text{OH}^-$$

Calculate the standard cell potential of this cell. (The final answer is a value)
